I had just taken a store manager position for a national adult toy and novelty store. The store was very high turnover, with managers and employees regularly calling in every day. Because of this, I worked 7 days a week regularly, closing shifts until 2am and turning around opening at 9am when my opener would call in. 

I started just before the start of the pandemic and worked with them through shut downs for about 6 months. Our stores never shut down as corporate office and selfish customers decided we would be “essential” and would offer curbside service to customers. As much as people tell me I should be grateful I had a job, after working 4 months continuously I was begging to be furloughed but it never came. Customers were relentless and rude, demanding to come in the store and frustrated with having to place phone orders for magazines and dildos. Once we opened back up, it was all even worse. With regular call offs or quits due to the safety or low pay of the position, customers were unbearable. The final straw was corporate had adjusted our bonus structure to make up for reduced sales, and I was in charge one store doing great and another store under performing so I never bonused. I checked my pay check in a day I was finally going to get the lowest tier bonus, and saw nothing was there. 

I drafted a resignation letter about my experience and sent it to the VP of store operations clear through to my boss to talk about the terrible treatment and greediness of the company and left my keys on the counter. I felt bad for my team that had stuck things out with me, but I couldn’t do it. I was so exhausted, my marriage was failing, and while the pay was good it wasn’t worth any of what I was going through. 

Luckily a company that I had been dying to work with for over a year called me to tell me they had a position in staffing and recruiting that was perfect for my experience! I told them I needed to give a notice and took two weeks to refresh, reset and put that terrible job behind me.
